title: API client requirements
idea: Scoping an API client means deciding which failures to retry, which requests are safe to repeat, how long a call may take, and when to stop calling.
points: Retry only transient failures: timeouts, connection errors, 503 and similar.
Repeat a request only if it is idempotent or carries an Idempotency-Key.
Every call has a per-attempt timeout and a total time budget.
A circuit breaker fails fast while a downstream service keeps failing.

hero.title: Actors and use cases in v1

edges.caption: The caller asks for one logical call. It should not care how many attempts happen underneath.

edges.label: on failure
edges.caption: A transient failure on a safe request triggers another attempt after a growing, randomised wait.

edges.label: always
edges.caption: Each attempt has its own timeout, and all attempts together share one total budget.

edges.label: feeds
edges.caption: Repeated failures trip the breaker. Later calls fail at once instead of piling onto a sick service.
An operator sets policies per downstream service, for example fewer attempts for a slow one.

edges.label: used by
edges.caption: The client reads the policy for the service it is calling.

edges.label: defers
edges.caption: Caching, hedging and cross-host breaker state are cut from v1. Say so out loud.

code.title: The retry rule as code
code.caption: Six failed calls run through the v1 retry rule, then the use cases are listed with their actor and scope.

walk.text: Six failed calls: method, failure kind, and whether an Idempotency-Key was sent.
Each failure kind says whether it may succeed if tried again.
A request is safe to repeat if its method is idempotent or it has a key.
Retry needs both: a transient failure and a request safe to repeat.
Five use cases form v1, across caller, client and operator.
Three are named and cut, so the boundary is visible in the design.

pitfalls: Never retry a plain POST; a lost response may hide a completed charge.
Do not retry 400 or 404; the same request fails the same way.
Agree on a total time budget, or retries can outlast the caller's own timeout.

quiz.q: A POST to create a payment times out. No Idempotency-Key was sent. What should v1 do?
options: Retry it up to the maximum attempts
Return the timeout to the caller without retrying
Retry once, since timeouts are transient
Switch the request to PUT and retry
quiz.why: The server may have charged before the timeout. Without a key it cannot spot the repeat, so a retry risks a double charge.

takeaway: Retry only transient failures, and only requests that are safe to repeat.

starters: Why is PUT idempotent but POST is not?
Should 429 Too Many Requests be retried?
Who should own the total timeout, the client or the caller?
